get.summary:
Lists tickets for the service provider using cursor pagination.
Default sort is `updatedOn desc`. sortBy accepts only
`updatedOn` or `createdOn`; sortOrder accepts only
`asc` or `desc` (case-insensitive) — any other value is rejected with a 400.

parameters.name: Cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page; omit for the first page.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description: Number of items per page. Clamped to 1–200 (default 50).

parameters.name: SortBy
parameters.description: Sort column: `updatedOn` (default) or `createdOn`.

parameters.name: SortOrder
parameters.description: Sort direction: `asc` or `desc` (default).

parameters.name: StatusIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated status ids to include. Omit for every status.

parameters.name: ClientIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated client ids to include. Omit for every client.

parameters.name: PriorityIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated priority ids on the public scale — None=0, Urgent=1, High=2, Normal=3, Low=4.

parameters.name: TypeIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated ticket type ids to include.

parameters.name: LeadAssigneeIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated lead assignee ids to include.

parameters.name: ContactIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated contact ids to include.

parameters.name: TagIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated tag ids; a ticket matches if it carries any of them.

parameters.name: GroupIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated group ids; a ticket matches if it is subscribed to any of them.

parameters.name: Query
parameters.description: Keyword matched against the ticket title, number and display number. Up to 200 characters.

parameters.name: UpdatedSince
parameters.description: ISO-8601 timestamp; keeps only tickets updated at or after it.

parameters.name: UpdatedBefore
parameters.description: ISO-8601 timestamp; keeps only tickets updated strictly before it.

parameters.name: CreatedSince
parameters.description: ISO-8601 timestamp; keeps only tickets created at or after it.

parameters.name: CreatedBefore
parameters.description: ISO-8601 timestamp; keeps only tickets created strictly before it.

post.summary:
Adds a comment to a ticket. The comment is always recorded as coming from the API — the
caller cannot post as a specific user, and `To` and `Cc` are taken from the
conversation rather than the request.

parameters.name: ticketId
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

get.summary:
Lists the comments on a ticket using cursor pagination. Comments read oldest-first by
default, like a conversation top to bottom.
Filter from broadest to narrowest: send nothing for every comment; conversationType
to select kinds; or conversationTypeId together with
conversationId for one specific conversation.

parameters.name: ticketId
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

parameters.name: ConversationType
parameters.description: Kinds to include: `1` Public, `2` Private, `3` Side Conversation, `4` Approval. Comma-separated on its own; a single value when paired with conversationId.

parameters.name: ConversationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the single conversation to read, from the conversations endpoint. Requires a single conversationType.

parameters.name: Cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page; omit for the first page.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description: Number of items per page. Clamped to 1–200 (default 50).

parameters.name: SortBy
parameters.description: Sort column: `createdOn`.

parameters.name: SortOrder
parameters.description: Sort direction: `asc` (default) or `desc`.

post.summary:
Uploads a single file to a ticket and returns its name and a temporary secure link. Pass
that name and link in a comment's `Attachments` when creating it.
Send the file as `multipart/form-data` in a field named `file`. Any file type is
accepted. This endpoint enforces no size rule of its own; a large file is rejected earlier
by the infrastructure in front of it, which answers 413 rather than a validation error.

parameters.name: ticketId
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

get.summary:
Lists the conversations on a ticket. Public and Private are the ticket's main thread and
come back with a null `Id`; Side Conversation and Approval carry a real `Id` that
can be passed to the comments endpoint as `conversationId`.
Type-specific details live on each type's own detail endpoint, so every row has the same
lean shape.

parameters.name: ticketId
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

get.summary:
Gets a single comment on a ticket. Same shape as a comments-list item except that the full
`BodyHtml` is always included, so there is no `BodyTruncated` field.

parameters.name: ticketId
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

parameters.name: commentId
parameters.description: Comment identifier.

get.summary:
Gets a single approval on a ticket, with its approvers. This is where approval status
lives — the conversations list stays lean and does not carry it. `Status` is worked
out from the approvers: Disapproved as soon as anyone disapproves, Approved once everyone
approves, Pending otherwise.

parameters.name: ticketId
parameters.description: Ticket identifier.

parameters.name: approvalId
parameters.description: Approval identifier, from the conversations endpoint.

BillingName.description: Optional name used on invoices when it differs from the display name.

Domain.description: Optional primary web domain for the client (e.g. contoso.com).

public-cluster_PublicApprovalDetailModel.description:
Full details of one approval on a ticket — this is where approval status lives, the
conversations list being deliberately lean. Attachments belong to the approval's comments
rather than to the approval itself, so there is no attachments field here. Timestamps are UTC.

ContactId.description: Identifier of the contact asked to approve.

public-cluster_PublicApproverModel.description:
One person's response on an approval.
            
There is deliberately no response timestamp here. The approver document carries a
`submittedAt`, but it is written once when the approver is created and is never
rewritten when they answer — every decided approver observed on Dev carried a
`submittedAt` within 130ms of its approval's creation. Exposing it would publish a
creation time under a name that promises a response time.
